messages.author: 5b55811f2e3aab0a
messages.subject: specifying level of replication in gpagen and other functions
parts:
Hi everyone,

I hope it's been a happy holiday season for all.

I have a question about how to specify the level of replication in gpagen and other functions in geomorph.

The problem I face is the following:

Specifically, I have samples from 11 populations (5 from habitat type A, 6 from habitat type B), with approximately 60-90 individuals from each population and all are identified as male or female.

My first question is, how can I compute separate mean (consensus) configurations and standard errors for each habitat type, such that each one is a mean of the population means? I understand that gpagen computes the mean configuration for each group (in my case, habitat type) by pooling individuals within that group, ignoring the population factor. So in other words, can  gpagen be used to compute a mean of the population means, as well as standard errors? If not, would it be legitimate to repeat the process twice? (i.e. once for each population, then again for each habitat type using population means).

Also, if the above is possible, would it be anymore complicated to do this separately for males and females in each habitat type?

I know that in procD.lm and advanced.procD.lm, I can specify at least two factors, but as far as I can see, the mean configuration is computed by pooling individuals at the specified level.

My concern over this is because I have been advised to use the mean of means for my analyses to avoid issues with pseudo-replication. Also, it seems that pooling individuals from all populations within a habitat type is not advisable because of the obvious effect that sample size has on standard errors, especially if the mean +/- se is computed for 5 observations vs 500 observations.

Looking forward to your responses.


Kind regards,

Daniel

messages.author: 91722721526eb1d7
messages.subject: Re: specifying level of replication in gpagen and other functions
parts:
Hi Daniel,

To calculate the mean shape for a group, simply use the geomorph::mshape function as follows (using a geomorph example):

data(plethodon) 

Y.gpa <- gpagen(plethodon$land,PrinAxes=FALSE) # perform GPA


# get mean shapes for the two species in plethodon$species factor

plethodon$species

 [1] Jord  Jord  Jord  Jord  Jord  Jord  Jord  Jord  Jord  Jord  Teyah Teyah Teyah Teyah Teyah

[16] Teyah Teyah Teyah Teyah Teyah Jord  Jord  Jord  Jord  Jord  Jord  Jord  Jord  Jord  Jord 

[31] Teyah Teyah Teyah Teyah Teyah Teyah Teyah Teyah Teyah Teyah

Levels: Jord Teyah


mean.Jord <- mshape(Y.gpa$coords[,,which(plethodon$species == "Jord")])

mean.Teyah <- mshape(Y.gpa$coords[,,which(plethodon$species == "Teyah")])


# Or using the function geomorph::coords.subset


new.coords <- coords.subset(A = Y.gpa$coords, group = plethodon$species)

# new.coords is a list length 2, with two 3D arrays for the two levels, named by the level name, so:


mean.Jord <- mshape(new.coords$Jord)

mean.Teyah <- mshape(new.coords$Teyah)


# To view:

plotRefToTarget(mean.Jord, mean.Jord, method = "points") # mean shape on own

plotRefToTarget(Y.gpa$consensus, mean.Jord, method = "TPS") # as a shape change from the overall mean


Emma

messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Re: specifying level of replication in gpagen and other functions
parts:
And yet a third way to do the same thing…

Use coords.subset and mshape

data("plethodon")
Y.gpa <- gpagen(plethodon$land)
lapply(coords.subset(Y.gpa$coords, plethodon$species), mshape)

One could also quickly get means from separate GPAs done individually on groups

groupGPAs <- lapply(coords.subset(plethodon$land, plethodon$species), mshape)
groupGPAs

Of note, if one did the latter, the landmark VCVs could be extracted and SEs could be calculated, but any interpretation form such a thing should be done with caution.  In this case, landmark SEs are not purely attributed to natural variation at landmarks, but also the GPA procedure, itself.  

Mike

Hi all,

 I'm aware of those functions, and I just realized after reading my post again, that either I didn't correctly describe what I wanted to do or I misunderstood the techniques you suggested.

So the 3 or 4 techniques you described are for computing means for individuals subsetted by a factor i.e:
pop mean = GPA (1, 2, 3,...n individuals) or by ls.means or mshape, etc.
Where you have n individuals in each of a population.

I would like to do something different, based on my example from the previous post; 2 habitat types, 5 populations in each habitat type, ~60 specimens in each population):
i.e. mean of the means, so my level of replication is population rather than the individual (5 instead of 60)
habitat mean = GPA (1, 2, 3,...n population means)
Where you have n populations means computed via GPA on n individuals within each population.

This way my level of replication is not the individual, but the population, with 5 observations for each habitat type instead of ~60 individuals per population as I currently have.

In other words, is it possible to perform GPA for each population, and then perform a GPA again on those mean configurations?

Thanks again.

Also, if the above is possible, would it be anymore complicated to do this separately for males and females in each habitat type?

I know that in procD.lm and advanced.procD.lm, I can specify at least two factors, but as far as I can see, the mean configuration is computed by pooling individuals at the specified level.

My concern over this is because I have been advised to use the mean of means for my analyses to avoid issues with pseudo-replication. Also, it seems that pooling individuals from all populations within a habitat type is not advisable because of the obvious effect that sample size has on standard errors, especially if the mean +/- se is computed for 5 observations vs 500 observations.

Looking forward to your responses.


Kind regards,

Daniel

Daniel,

 

We did in fact understand your original question and its intent. Our responses were framed the way they were because what you wished to do and thought was an obvious way to go is not statistically legitimate, nor is it necessary.

 

Simply put, one should not perform separate GPA – superimpositions on different groups and then combine these data or some summaries of them in downstream analyses. That is the case for the individuals, or the means based on them. The reason is that each GPA will superimpose specimens to their own mean, but these are not aligned to an overall mean.  Thus, each dataset is a projected to a different rotation (projection) in tangent space, making them incompatible for subsequent analyses (see papers by Rohlf in the 1990s where this is discussed).


So instead, if one is interested in population means (or means from any grouping), the correct approach is to perform GPA on all specimens and then obtain group means from these aligned specimens. These will contain all of the shape differences between group means, which is embodied by their Procrustes distances to each other.

 

Interestingly, it turns out that nothing is gained by performing the second GPA on the group means obtained by first doing GPA on everyone.  If you keep the data in Shape space (not Tangent space), the correlation of distances between the original means, and the GPA-rotated means is precisely 1.0!  If you use the Tangent space coordinates, it won’t be exactly 1.0, but will be extremely close (~0.9998 or so), which reflects the projection-scaling step from Shape Space to Tangent Space.  R-code example is below for you.


So you see, the steps you wished to perform are superfluous, and one can get to where you wished to go using a single GPA of all specimens, followed by the calculation of group means from them.

 

Hope this makes things more clear.

 

Dean

 

library(geomorph)

data(plethodon)

Y.gpa<-gpagen(plethodon$land,Proj=FALSE)    #GPA-alignment

gdf <- geomorph.data.frame(Y.gpa, species = plethodon$species, site = plethodon$site)

means<-advanced.procD.lm(coords ~ site*species, ~ 1, groups = ~site*species,

                  iter=499, data = gdf)$LS.means

orig<-dist(means)

new<-dist(two.d.array(gpagen(arrayspecs(means,p=12,k=2),Proj=FALSE)$coords))

cor(orig,new)

So the 3 or 4 techniques you described are for computing means for individuals subsetted by a factor i.e:
pop mean = GPA (1, 2, 3,...n individuals) or by ls.means or mshape, etc.
Where you have n individuals in each of a population.

I would like to do something different, based on my example from the previous post; 2 habitat types, 5 populations in each habitat type, ~60 specimens in each population):
i.e. mean of the means, so my level of replication is population rather than the individual (5 instead of 60)
habitat mean = GPA (1, 2, 3,...n population means)
Where you have n populations means computed via GPA on n individuals within each population.

This way my level of replication is not the individual, but the population, with 5 observations for each habitat type instead of ~60 individuals per population as I currently have.

In other words, is it possible to perform GPA for each population, and then perform a GPA again on those mean configurations?

Sorry everybody, the last line should have used gpagen, not mshape; i.e.,  

 

groupGPAs <- lapply(coords.subset(plethodon$land, plethodon$species), gpagen)
groupGPAs
On Jan 10, 2017, at 7:08 PM, Mike Collyer <mlco...@gmail.com> wrote:

And yet a third way to do the same thing…

 

Use coords.subset and mshape

data("plethodon")

Y.gpa <- gpagen(plethodon$land)

lapply(coords.subset(Y.gpa$coords, plethodon$species), mshape)

 

One could also quickly get means from separate GPAs done individually on groups

 

groupGPAs <- lapply(coords.subset(plethodon$land, plethodon$species), mshape)

groupGPAs

 

Of note, if one did the latter, the landmark VCVs could be extracted and SEs could be calculated, but any interpretation form such a thing should be done with caution.  In this case, landmark SEs are not purely attributed to natural variation at landmarks, but also the GPA procedure, itself.  

 

Mike

Hi Daniel,

 

To calculate the mean shape for a group, simply use the geomorph::mshape function as follows (using a geomorph example):

 

data(plethodon) 

Y.gpa <- gpagen(plethodon$land,PrinAxes=FALSE) # perform GPA

 

# get mean shapes for the two species in plethodon$species factor

plethodon$species

 [1] Jord  Jord  Jord  Jord  Jord  Jord  Jord  Jord  Jord  Jord  Teyah Teyah Teyah Teyah Teyah

[16] Teyah Teyah Teyah Teyah Teyah Jord  Jord  Jord  Jord  Jord  Jord  Jord  Jord  Jord  Jord 

[31] Teyah Teyah Teyah Teyah Teyah Teyah Teyah Teyah Teyah Teyah

Levels: Jord Teyah

 

mean.Jord <- mshape(Y.gpa$coords[,,which(plethodon$species == "Jord")])

mean.Teyah <- mshape(Y.gpa$coords[,,which(plethodon$species == "Teyah")])

 

# Or using the function geomorph::coords.subset

 

new.coords <- coords.subset(A = Y.gpa$coords, group = plethodon$species)

# new.coords is a list length 2, with two 3D arrays for the two levels, named by the level name, so:

 

mean.Jord <- mshape(new.coords$Jord)

mean.Teyah <- mshape(new.coords$Teyah)

 

# To view:

plotRefToTarget(mean.Jord, mean.Jord, method = "points") # mean shape on own

plotRefToTarget(Y.gpa$consensus, mean.Jord, method = "TPS") # as a shape change from the overall mean

 

Emma
